answer.evidence: The stairs repeat in 8-row cycles: a 1-row light nosing line (rows 0, 8, 16, 24), then a gray brick-patterned face, then a dark shadow row (rows 7, 15, 23, 31). The light line sits at the top of each cycle with no separate lighter tread band behind it. The steps therefore read as stacked vertical riser faces, with only a 1-3 row highlight as the top. Rows 31-47 are a plain cobble wall face with no top surface. Edge columns show grass and dirt at the sides, but there is no receding side face. The whole piece is a front elevation, not a 3/4 view with visible horizontal treads.
